message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: .NET Linux

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "master" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "master" ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        submodules: recursive
        fetch-depth: 0

    - name: Setup .NET
      uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v3
      with:
        dotnet-version: 10.0.x

    - name: Cache NuGet packages
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.nuget/packages
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.csproj') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-

    - name: Restore dependencies
      run: dotnet restore GameRealisticMap-LinuxCI.sln

    - name: Build
      run: dotnet build --no-restore --configuration Release GameRealisticMap-LinuxCI.sln

    - name: Test
      run: dotnet test --no-build --verbosity normal --configuration Release GameRealisticMap-LinuxCI.sln
      
    - name: Build Linux Command Line
      run: dotnet publish --no-self-contained -f net10.0 -r linux-x64 -c Release GameRealisticMap.Arma3.CommandLine/GameRealisticMap.Arma3.CommandLine.csproj -o Output
      
    - name: Upload build artifacts
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: Linux Command Line
        path: Output/grma3",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs `dotnet restore` on every invocation with no dependency cache. Pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE supports caching dependency downloads to reduce repeated fetch work, with reported modest aggregate VM-time benefit. Preconditions are met: dependency fetching is repeated and measurable, and cache inputs can be keyed to project/lockfile files. No contraindications apply: there is no existing equivalent cache, and the cached NuGet package cache is not mutable or untrusted build output. All original build, test, publish, and artifact steps are preserved unchanged; only a cache step is inserted before restore.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
